newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets end flat but with firm undertone.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets end flat but with firm undertone.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
AUCKLAND, May 28 (Reuter) New Zealand debt markets ended barely changed on Wednesday after a strong run over the last few days.
Talk of further euro or samurai issuance kept the market interested, however.
"Definitely with the Australian dollar easing it makes euros and samurais more likely," said one dealer.
"It's not an outstanding performance but it has had a good few days," he said.
Bill futures were closing on their lows at around 92.98 for the June contract.
A correction down to the mid 92.80s or the low 92.90s, equating to a 10-15 basis point movement in the physical bill market, was a possibility, he said.
Most bill rates and bond yields were unchanged from Tuesday levels with longer bonds only slightly softer following a spike up in U.S. bond yields overnight.
